p1: Long ago, there were no phones or cars. Important news came with a messenger who ran on foot from town to town.
People waited and waited to hear the news. Would it be happy news or sad news?
Isaiah said the feet that bring good news over the mountains are beautiful! That news tells of peace.
p2: Why feet? Dusty, tired feet carried the happy news to the people. The best good news is about Jesus. The Book of Mormon teaches this is about Jesus and all who share Him.
Your feet can carry good news too. Tonight, tell someone you love, “Jesus loves you!”
old: Long ago there were no phones and no mail. When there was news, a person had to run and carry it on his own two feet, all the way over the mountains. Isaiah was a prophet, and he saw a runner coming over the hills with good news. "How beautiful are his feet!" Isaiah said. Dusty running feet are not pretty - but Isaiah meant that the news those feet carried was so happy it made the feet beautiful.

Heavenly Father's people had been taken far away from home to a land called Babylon, and they had waited and waited to go back. The good news the runner carried was this: "Heavenly Father is the King! Peace is coming! You are going home safe!" Isaiah was talking about Jesus too. Jesus is the One who brings us home safe to Heavenly Father.
Watchmen were men who stood up high on the city wall to watch for anyone coming. When the watchmen saw that runner, they could not keep quiet. They shouted and sang together, all at the same time.

The city of Jerusalem had been knocked down, and only broken old walls were left. Isaiah said even those broken stones would sing - because Heavenly Father had wrapped His people in comfort, the way a warm blanket wraps you.

Scout had good news too. The baby hamsters were born! Scout ran outside on two fast feet to tell everyone. You can be a runner like that. When you carry something kind and true to someone - "I love you," "you can play with me," "Jesus loves you" - your little feet are beautiful to Heavenly Father.
